`benmore upload <file> --app <name> [--kind media|feedback] [--type <mime>]` adds one local file to the app's dashboard media library on the hosted platform (the library `benmore media <app>` lists), not to the app's own uploads/ storage. The CLI asks the platform for an upload address that expires after 5 minutes, sends the bytes straight to storage and confirms; it prints JSON with `id`, `url` (the permanent address), `read_url` (a direct link valid for one hour), `size` and `mime`. `--kind media` (the default) accepts PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, SVG and PDF files up to 25 MB; `--kind feedback` accepts PNG, JPEG and WebP up to 5 MB; anything else is refused before a byte is sent. `--type` gives the content type; without it the type comes from the file extension, and an extension that gives none exits 1. Editor access. The library belongs to the app, so `--env` is accepted and changes nothing.

`benmore upload-url <app> <path> [--env dev|prod]` (MCP generate_upload_url) answers `upload_url`, `path` and `static_url`: a link to give to a person, who opens it in a browser and drops one file. The file is stored as `static/<path>` in the selected instance and served at `/static/<path>`. The link works once, within 15 minutes, for a file of at most 5 MB, and only while the account that made it keeps editor access. `<path>` is relative to static/ (a leading `/` or `static/` is dropped): 1 to 256 characters, each segment made of letters, digits, spaces and `. - _ ( ) + @`. With no `--env` and no pin the CLI targets prod once the app has a prod instance, else dev (the MCP tool targets dev when the app has one).
